correctness.rationale: A unitary reflection/dilation gives a self-adjoint Hankel kernel. The trace-class integral decomposition through R_t J_t^2 bounds the whole kernel Taylor remainder by O(alpha^-2) in nuclear norm. Exact exponential moments yield one +1/8 and one -1/8 first-order eigenvalue. Finite-rank perturbation and nuclear error control all remaining singular values. The nuclear best rank-one error follows from singular-value truncation. The reproducibility checker confirms moments and separate finite Nyström values.

originality.rationale: Eveson 2003 gives only leading trace norm and explicitly raises the O(1/n) rank-one nuclear error question, proving a weaker O(n^-1/2+epsilon) bound; the new statement gives the first sharp constant and nuclear O(n^-2) residual. Earlier visible results on operator/HS norm and first two singular values do not imply a nuclear remainder: square-summability has no sum bound. Closest scientific sources and searched aliases did not establish the same implication. Residual historical priority risk acknowledged.
residual_risks: An equivalent historical result could use Hankel/Volterra trace-norm nomenclature not captured by searched aliases.
The full text of Thorpe 1998 was not obtained; abstract alone cannot justify whole-document noncoverage.

value.rationale: The paper motivating this family expressly asks for improved rate of the best nuclear rank-one approximation. The exact first-order coefficient 1/8, the global trace coefficient 1/4 and proof of an S1-sized remainder resolve that natural operator-ideal question, distinguishing nuclear control from known first-mode/HS asymptotics. The result is a meaningful quantitative strengthening and an additional reusable Hankel decomposition, without claiming a whole new family.
